events.title: Sachsen-Anhalt Parliamentary Election Winner
events.description:
Parliamentary elections to elect the Landtag of Sachsen-Anhalt are scheduled to take place on September 6, 2026.

This market will resolve to the political party that wins the greatest number of seats in the state parliament of Sachsen-Anhalt (Landtag) as a result of this election.

If voting in the Sachsen-Anhalt election for the Landtag does not occur by January 31, 2027, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party that received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed abbreviation appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as published on the official website of the Landtag of Sachsen-Anhalt (https://www.landtag.sachsen-anhalt.de/).

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent polls ahead of the September 6, 2026, Sachsen-Anhalt Landtag election show the AfD maintaining a commanding lead at 40-43%, roughly double its 2021 result of 20.8%, while the incumbent CDU has fallen to 22-23%.** Multiple surveys from Infratest dimap, Forschungsgruppe Wahlen, and others confirm this consistent gap, driven by sustained voter shifts in the eastern state and limited movement among smaller parties. The CDU-SPD-FDP government faces notable losses, with the Left, SPD, and Greens projected to enter parliament but at levels insufficient to close the gap. Late undecided voters (11-31% in recent samples) and turnout variations remain the primary variables, yet the scale of the AfD’s advantage leaves little room for reversal before election day. Trader consensus at 99.7% for an AfD plurality win aligns with these polling trends and the short remaining timeline.

This market will resolve to the political party that wins the second greatest number of seats in the state parliament of Sachsen-Anhalt (Landtag) as a result of this election.

If voting in the Sachsen-Anhalt election for the Landtag does not occur by January 31, 2027, this market will resolve to "Other".

The named parties or coalitions will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more parties are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid second votes received (Zweitstimme), with higher vote totals ranking higher. If parties remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed party abbreviations. This market will resolve to the party that occupies the second finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as published on the official website of the Landtag of Sachsen-Anhalt (https://www.landtag.sachsen-anhalt.de/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent polling ahead of the September 6 Sachsen-Anhalt Landtag election shows the AfD leading with 40-43 percent, positioning the CDU as the clear second-place contender at 22-23 percent. The Left trails at 11-13 percent, with the SPD, Greens, and others further behind or near the five-percent threshold. This gap reflects the CDU’s established voter base as the incumbent governing party, sustained name recognition for Minister-President Sven Schulze, and limited recent momentum for challengers despite the AfD’s gains. Traders’ near-certain pricing for a CDU second-place finish aligns with these stable survey trends. A late surge by The Left or unexpected turnout shifts among undecided voters could narrow the margin, though such movement has not materialized in the final week of campaigning.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent polls from late August 2026 consistently project the AfD at 40–43% in the September 6 state election, short of the roughly 50%+ needed for an absolute majority (42 of 83 seats) in the Sachsen-Anhalt Landtag.** 

Forschungsgruppe Wahlen (ZDF) and Infratest dimap (ARD) surveys place the AfD well ahead of the CDU (22–23%), followed by the Left (11–13%), SPD (8–9%), and Greens (5–6%), with BSW and FDP typically below the 5% threshold. These distributions leave the AfD short of a majority even in higher estimates, as additional parties entering parliament fragments the seat allocation. 

The AfD, classified as “gesichert rechtsextrem” by the state Verfassungsschutz, faces a firm firewall: all other parties have ruled out coalitions, forcing reliance on an outright majority that current polling does not support. AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund has explicitly targeted sole government, but recent surveys and undecided-voter levels (around 30%) have not shifted the outlook enough to close the gap. 

With the election one week away, these stable late-August figures underpin the strong trader consensus against an AfD absolute majority.

Traders reflect this gap in implied probabilities, with Dallas favored amid SKC’s ongoing defensive and results struggles.

eventMetadata.context_description: Seattle Sounders FC host New York Red Bulls at Lumen Field in an MLS regular-season fixture on September 5-6, 2026. Seattle enters amid a prolonged injury crisis that has sidelined multiple contributors, including forward Jesús Ferreira (hamstring), defender Yeimar Gómez Andrade (calf, 4-6 weeks), and others with hamstring or hip issues, contributing to a recent extended losing streak and roster strain under coach Brian Schmetzer. The Red Bulls sit mid-table in the Eastern Conference with a record near 7-9-4, hampered by their own absences such as goalkeeper A.J. Marcucci (knee) and questions around Rafael Mosquera, while showing inconsistent results including recent road losses. Home advantage and historical patterns favor the Sounders when healthy, yet current roster limitations and travel factors shape trader assessments of the matchup.

eventMetadata.context_description: Tigres UANL enter the Liga MX Apertura 2026 clash as clear favorites, buoyed by a recent 2-0 victory over Atlante that ended a lengthy winless run and the appointment of interim manager Víctor Manuel Vucetich. Key contributors like Juan Brunetta, Ángel Correa, Diego Lainez, and Rodrigo Aguirre provide attacking depth and creativity, supported by a more organized defense. Necaxa, coming off a 1-1 draw with Pumas and a narrow loss to León, continue to show inconsistency and defensive vulnerabilities on the road. Historical head-to-head results heavily favor Tigres, who have dominated recent meetings. Home advantage at Estadio Universitario, combined with Necaxa’s struggles to secure results away from Aguascalientes, shapes trader expectations around the match outcome and goal markets.

This market will resolve to "Over" if Khomenko Maksym and Storozhenko Oleksandr combine to play 4 or more total games in the match. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "Under".
For the purposes of this market, total games are calculated using all games played across the full match. Any forfeited points or games will count toward final settlement.
If the match is completed, this market will resolve based on the final completed match score. If a player retires, withdraws, is defaulted, is disqualified, or the match otherwise begins but is not completed, this market will resolve based on any outcome that was already unequivocally determined at the time play stopped.
For total games markets, an outcome is considered determined if it would have been guaranteed had the match been played to completion using the minimum number of additional games required. For example, if a total games market is Over/Under 3.5 and play stops with the score 2-1 in games, the players have played 3 total games, and the minimum completed score would require one additional game, resulting in at least 4 total games. Therefore, Over 3.5 would resolve as the winning outcome. If the market were Over/Under 4.5, the outcome would not be guaranteed and would resolve 50-50.
If neither outcome was already determined at the time play stopped, this market will resolve 50-50. If the match is canceled before play begins or delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without play beginning, this market will resolve 50-50.
Resolution will be based on official Setka Cup results.

eventMetadata.context_description:
Both LA Galaxy and New England Revolution enter the September 5 matchup with depleted attacking options and mixed recent form that has produced low-scoring, hard-to-predict results. Galaxy sit 12th in the West (6-8-8, 26 points) after a 1-0 win over San Jose while playing shorthanded, but they remain winless in most home fixtures amid long-term absences for Riqui Puig, João Klauss, and Erik Thommy plus additional knocks to Elijah Wynder and others. Revolution hold fourth in the East (10-3-7, 33 points) with a solid defensive record but have leaned on limited depth following extended absences for Leonardo Campana and Ilay Feingold. 

These roster constraints, combined with Galaxy’s inconsistent finishing and Revolution’s variable away output, have left traders viewing most specific scorelines as roughly equiprobable, reflecting broad uncertainty over whether either side can generate the clean attacking sequences needed for higher tallies.
